description: Facts shared by the CSF and AI RMF tracks: the intake menus (scripts/intake.py turns the typed numbers into these values), the domains and certifications, and the question types in order of how demanding they are. Read through scripts/options.py; no script keeps its own copy.

questions.prompt: Certifications held (pick all that apply, e.g. "2 3")

options.label: None - no AI in use or planned
Some - AI is in use, or being built or piloted
Unsure - not known (shadow use is possible)

questions.prompt: Do you build AI, use AI, or both?

options.label: Use - you use AI built by others (including vendor AI and AI in the tools you use)
Build - you own a model (built from scratch, or trained / tuned on an existing model)
Both

questions.prompt: Is your model built on an existing model (trained or tuned from it)?

options.label: Yes
No - built from scratch

questions.prompt: Do you give the model to others (clients, partners, an API, devices, open weights)?

options.label: Yes
No - used only by your own org

questions.prompt: How do you use AI? (pick all that apply, or leave blank)

options.label: Internal process - AI output used in internal decisions and workflows (HR, finance, approvals, operations)
Code generation - AI writes or maintains your applications
Customer-facing application - AI in an app, or output reaching customers
Vendor AI - vendors and products you use run AI on your data (Jira, Slack, ServiceNow, GitHub, RPA ...)

questions.prompt: What does your AI include? (pick all that apply, or leave blank)

options.label: RAG / knowledge graph - the AI reads your data to answer
MCP / tools - the AI can call tools, hosted by you or outside
Agents - the AI acts with little human oversight (MCP / tools are then included)
A model you host yourself (including a PoC on your own infrastructure)

questions.prompt: Is the CSF assessment part of this engagement and done before the AI RMF assessment?

options.label: Yes
No
Yes
No
